name: Hydrus
introduction: is the Lesser Water Snake, introduced by Dutch navigators in the 1590s. It winds between the two Magellanic Clouds near the south celestial pole and never rises for most northern observers.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Beta Hydri](hip:2021), 24 light-years away, offers a glimpse of the Sun’s future. It is a star slightly more massive than the Sun and several billion years older, which has begun to swell into a subgiant as its core hydrogen runs low.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Hydri](hip:9236) is a white star 63 light-years away, near Achernar. [Gamma Hydri](hip:17678) is a red giant near the Large Magellanic Cloud.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Large and Small Magellanic Clouds lie on either side of Hydrus, so the snake winds between two neighboring galaxies.
